clue.text: Problems after man leads navy round very hot part of England

indicators.note: problems come after the rest, so their synonym goes at the end
man leads navy, so the word for man comes first and the navy abbreviation follows
the man-and-navy string is placed round the abbreviation for very, enclosing it

parts.note: a man is a male
RN is the Royal Navy
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ills are problems or troubles

explanation.surface: A route description: past a man and the navy, round a scorching stretch of English countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Malvern Hills are a range in Worcestershire and Herefordshire, a geographical region within England.

clue.text: Independent supporting a religious leader from general principles

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it goes after

parts.note: a prior heads a priory of monks

explanation.surface: An independent politician backs a church leader, perhaps on principle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supporting' means sitting underneath, so I comes after A PRIOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from theory or axioms rather than from observed experience.

clue.text: Wrong to limit ordinary opinion

indicators.note: to limit is to hem in, so the word for wrong encloses the other letter

parts.note: a vice is a moral wrong
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: It is wrong to restrict the views of ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a voice in something is to have a say, an expressed view on the matter.

clue.text: Staff getting over adopting new musical movement

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the staff word holds the letter for new

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Staff recovering from something while taking on a new piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a form in which a recurring theme alternates with episodes, often a sonata's last movement.

clue.text: Henry left party — old King identifying this exit?

parts.note: Hal is the familiar name of Prince Henry in Shakespeare's history plays
a do is a party
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Henry left the party, and the old king wonders which door he used.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints Henry leaving a party through the door of the hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall door is a front entrance opening into the hall, and so a way out of the house.

clue.text: View showing first and last of lighthouses on headland

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the first letter of lighthouses is L and the last is S, read literally as L AND S
a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A seascape with lighthouses standing on a promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'and' is kept as letters: the first and last of lighthouses gives L, AND, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a stretch of scenery seen in one sweep, or a painting of it.

clue.text: Arousing stuff? No good shunning lusting — I'm aroused

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
shunning means avoiding, so those letters are left out of the word

explanation.surface: A racy confession: rejecting worthless lust, yet admitting to being aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking NG from LUSTING leaves LUSTI; add IM and 'aroused' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that provoke a response, so whimsically they are stuff that arouses.

clue.text: I prophesied a majority? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: most means the majority, the greater part

explanation.surface: A boast of having forecast a majority, nearly right.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the prophet's own voice: 'I prophesied' is Amos describing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos was an Old Testament prophet whose sayings form the Book of Amos.

clue.text: Skill I observed in chap describing another planet

indicators.note: the letters are seen within the chap word, so they go inside it

parts.note: a chap is a man
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A man with a skill for describing other worlds, like a science-fiction writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Martian is the adjective relating to Mars, a planet other than Earth.

clue.text: What comes after a flight is a pause between flights

definitions.meaning: the touchdown of an aircraft at the end of its journey
the flat area between two flights of stairs

explanation.definitionFit: Landing means both an aircraft's arrival and the level platform where a staircase turns.

clue.text: Nobleman, note, included in fifth level?

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the phrase for the level

parts.note: grade E is the fifth grade after A, B, C and D

explanation.surface: A noble rated only middling, with a note included in his assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee was a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank, now any eminent person.

clue.text: Very chilly pass in high surroundings

indicators.note: one word set in the other's surroundings goes inside it
the high word forms the surroundings, wrapping round the pass

parts.note: stoned means high on drugs
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A mountain pass high up, where it is bitterly cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like a description of the pass's altitude but means intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-cold means completely cold, as cold as stone, so extremely chilly.

clue.text: An American backed importing a Finnish bath

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the reversed string takes in the extra letter
backed means read backwards, so the two words are reversed together

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: An American has supported bringing in a Finnish bathing custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a steam bath of Finnish origin, the word itself being Finnish.

clue.text: Animation image incorporating infrared

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into the body, so the image word encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: the spit, as in the spitting image, means an exact likeness

explanation.surface: A cartoon image built using infrared technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animation' suggests cartoons but here means liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit and animation both mean liveliness, energy and vivacity.

clue.text: Fish product for those at sea (not hard)

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not means without, so the letter for hard is removed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A soft fish dish suited to sailors, rather than something hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H from FOR THOSE leaves FORTOSE, which 'at sea' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft roe is the milt of a male fish, eaten as food, so a product from fish.

clue.text: Source of wipeout unfortunately near skier

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A wipeout is unluckily close for a skier on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wipeout' is a skiing crash in the surface but here means erasing writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ink eraser removes ink marks, so it is the cause of the writing being wiped out.

clue.text: Scientist representing flair on DNA links, right?

indicators.note: representing means presenting again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist with a talent for DNA connections, fittingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram covers all the letters but the opening R. Fittingly, Franklin's X-ray work on DNA was key to finding its structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosalind Franklin was a British chemist whose X-ray diffraction images revealed the double helix.

clue.text: Discourage a director absorbed by dead topic

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as on gravestones and family trees

indicators.note: absorbed means taken in, so the topic word encloses the other letters

parts.note: an issue is a topic for discussion

explanation.surface: A director buried in a dull subject loses heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissuade someone is to talk them out of an action, putting them off it.

clue.text: See 16
Relief mission, perhaps, bearing a bit of alcohol?

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing
a drop is a small amount of drink

explanation.surface: An aid mission carrying a little liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: An airdrop delivers supplies by parachute, typically as part of a relief operation, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Happen a storm will sink a famous ship

parts.note: to be is to happen or take place

indicators.note: sinking means going under and out of sight, so the letter disappears from the storm word

parts.note: a gale is a storm

explanation.surface: A storm may come and sink a celebrated vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Beagle was the ship that carried Charles Darwin on his voyage round the world.

clue.text: Adduce Beethoven's Ninth, say, on reflection, describing variation in form?

indicators.note: reflection reverses an image, so the whole string reads backwards

parts.note: to adduce evidence is to cite it

indicators.note: ninth means the ninth letter of the word that follows

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: Quoting Beethoven's Ninth Symphony when thinking about variations on a theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ninth' looks like the symphony but takes the ninth letter of BEETHOVEN, N. CITE+N+EG read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic differences cause physical variation between organisms; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Contributions to tutor are reasonably less common

indicators.note: each word contributes some letters to the answer, which spans the phrase

explanation.surface: Reasonable contributions to a tutor are becoming scarcer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarer is the comparative of rare, meaning found or occurring less often.

clue.text: Resident mostly irritable about curtailed trip

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened irritable word wraps round the other
mostly means most of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sore means irritable or aggrieved

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a journey is a trip

explanation.surface: A resident grumbling about a trip that was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourner stays somewhere for a time, a temporary resident.

clue.text: Japanese move ousting British arbiter

indicators.note: ousting means driving out and taking the place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

explanation.surface: A Japanese decision that pushes out the British referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge decides disputes or contests, exactly what an arbiter does.

clue.text: Some hesitation over bikini top's shade

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation
the top half of a bikini is a bra

explanation.surface: Wavering over the colour of a bikini top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' looks like a colour, but means shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the darkest central part of a shadow, especially in an eclipse.

clue.text: Expect going topless will reveal evidence of neglect

indicators.note: losing its top means the first letter of the down entry is removed

parts.note: to trust is to expect confidently, as in I trust you will

explanation.surface: A cheeky warning that going topless will expose someone's neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust forms on iron left uncared for, so it shows something has been neglected.

clue.text: Regret backing areas, including South Island, as large land mass

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: the two area letters enclose the others

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Sorry to support regions, including an island in the south, as a vast continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is Europe and Asia taken together as one continuous continent.

clue.text: Argues children should receive bill, perversely

indicators.note: perversely means the wrong way round, so the result reads backwards
receiving means taking in, so the children word encloses the bill

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants
a tab is a bill, as in pick up the tab

explanation.surface: Insisting, contrarily, that the children pay the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Debates means discusses opposing views formally, so argues points out.

clue.text: Preserve and can ineptly? Everyone initially keeping at it

indicators.note: done ineptly, the letters are clumsily jumbled
initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Bungling the jam-making and canning, yet everyone keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' looks like the containment signal, but 'keeping at it' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Perseverance is steady persistence in a task despite difficulty, sticking with it.
